pinterest.title: Wedding witnesses and signing the certificates in Australia
pinterest.description: Section 44 of the Marriage Act 1961 requires at least 2 witnesses who are, or appear to the celebrant to be, over 18. On the day, the two of you, your celebrant and your witnesses sign 3 marriage certificates. Build a pause for the signing into your run sheet and check every name before anyone leaves. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

slides: What does your celebrant legally have to say in Australia? Less than you think. Swipe for the words.

The monitum. A celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says it before you marry. It opens: "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law". Marriage Act 1961, section 46(1). General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

The legal vow. Each of you says it to the other, before the celebrant and witnesses: "I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, A.B. (or C.D.), take thee, C.D. (or A.B.), to be my lawful wedded wife (or husband, or spouse)"; or words to that effect. Marriage Act 1961, section 45(2). General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
"Or words to that effect." Both legal passages end this way. Ask your celebrant before you change a word, and add your personal vows beside the legal line, not in place of it.

Witnesses and signing. At least 2 witnesses who are, or appear to the celebrant to be, over 18. The two of you, your celebrant and your witnesses sign 3 marriage certificates on the day. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

Marrying abroad? An Australian-authorised celebrant cannot perform an overseas marriage. Couples marry under the destination's law, or marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony abroad. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
Everything else is yours: the welcome, the reading, the ring words and the order of the optional parts. The full script, every line marked legally required or optional, is on the blog.
Planning the celebration around it, with guests flying in and a venue to secure? Talk to a Wedded Advisor about the venue, travel and vendors. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
The legal part of an Australian wedding ceremony is one statement from your celebrant, one sentence from each of you and a row of signatures. The rest, from the first welcome to the walk back down the aisle, is yours to write.

Our new guide puts the Marriage Act 1961 wording inside an original ceremony script, with every line marked legally required or optional: the section 46(1) monitum, the section 45(2) vow, your personal vows, the ring exchange, the signing and the presentation. There is also a short legal script for a small ceremony at home before a celebration abroad.

Read your personal vows to your celebrant before the day, and ask before you change any of the legal words.

If the ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, a Wedded Advisor from Wedded Concierge can plan the venue, travel and vendors around it as your single point of contact. Tell us where you are celebrating in the comments, or tap the link in bio to read the full script.

General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
